messages.subject: Profiling Stan Models?
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering how you guys profile Stan programs? I did not find anything on the wiki. Is there anything I need to particularly need to consider with profiling Stan programs or can I just go off and search for "profiling C++ programs"?

Thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Profiling Stan Models?
parts:
I haven't profiled all of Stan in a while, so someone
should definitely take a look.

The main obstacle is that inlining at high optimization
levels makes it hard to get a fine-grained view of where
time is going. If you don't optimize, then the timing info
isn't accurate.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Profiling Stan Models?
parts:
> On Jul 3, 2015, at 3:55 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hmmm... do you think a high level of optimization is also needed to just get a rough overview?

Yes, it's a factor of 10 or so in our code. We wrote it
with the optimizer in mind. Operations that look expensive
at -O0 can be compiled away (and thus free) at -O3.

But even profiling with compilation at -O3 can be expensive,
as some operations are intercepted and issues like the cost
of exceptions and some branching can be very hard to interpret.
Which is awful, because that's often where the high costs are.

If you find out anything useful in your spelunking, please let
us know. We should be profiling ourselves more often.

- Bob
